description:
Beef Trail Falls are situated on the traditional and unceded territory of the Ulkatcho First Nation. The Ulkatcho Carrier name for this area is Lhetungooh Nainli - pronounced Lhe / tun / gooh Nain / li, with the slash marks marking breaks between syllables. Lhetungooh refers to Beef Trail, while Nainli is the Ulkatcho word for waterfalls.

The trail is about 2.1 km in length from Beef Trail Road to the viewpoint for the waterfalls and takes most people about 45 minutes to complete each way (or 1.5 hours return). There are no facilities on the trail, so please plan accordingly.

Picturesque basalt (volcanic) rock formations line the edges of Beef Trail Creek; this area is part of the Anahim Volcanic Belt, a west-east trending chain of volcanoes and related magmatic features that is about 330 km (210 mi) long, extending from the Central Coast through the Coast Mountains to near the community of Nazko on the Interior Plateau.

This trail is not patrolled. There are hazards present along the trail, including steep banks and drop-offs, and fast flowing water. Please keep pets on a leash and keep small children under close supervision for their safety.

Please treat lightly while visiting this area and be sure to pack out everything you brought with you to help keep this area as beautiful and natural as possible.
directions:
Trail head Lat 52?38'36.41"N, Long 125?32'58.24"W

Beef Trail Falls are located northwest of the community of Anahim Lake, BC. To reach the start of the trail into Beef Trail Falls, travel west on Hwy 20 from the junction of Hwy 20 and Anahim Airport Road for about 15.7 km and then turn right / north onto the Beef Trail FSR. Travel about 13.5 km up the Beef Trail FSR to a pullout just before the bridge over Beef Trail Creek and park here. There is another wide spot for parking about 150 meters north of the bridge as well. The marked trailhead is on the north side of the bridge on the west side of the road.

stats.Closure:
NOTICE: The Beef Trail Road that provides the only vehicle access to the recreation trail is currently closed to support a Motor Vehicle Hunting Closed Area (MVHCA) under the Wildlife Act. It is anticipated the gate at the start of the Beef Trail Road on the north side of Highway 20 will remain closed throughout hunting season, so there will be no vehicle access to the recreation trail during this time.

For more detailed information on the specific areas where motor vehicles are closed for hunting, individuals can refer to the Wildlife Act Motor Vehicle Prohibition Regulation and the Hunting and Trapping Regulations Synopsis. These resources provide comprehensive details on the regulations and maps outlining the closed areas.
